mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) crosses above 8.5%, indicating a weakening labor market, this triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when UNRATE crosses above 8.5% threshold.

mechanism_narrative: Strong simultaneous growth in both demand (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) proxies indicates a robust economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days as market optimism drives equity valuations higher.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 60-day returns not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (rising FEDFUNDS), elevated discount rates reduce the present value of future equity cash flows, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during periods classified as monetary tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the supply index (INDPRO below 95.0) signals potential overcapacity or weak demand, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days as investors anticipate economic slowdown.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when INDPRO crosses below 95.0.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent high unemployment (UNRATE up) and falling employment (PAYEMS down) reflect a tightening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over 60 days due to reduced consumer spending and corporate profitability concerns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns not significantly negative (p > 0.05) despite the combined UNRATE and PAYEMS signals.

mechanism_narrative: Long-term upward trend in demand (GDPC1) reflects robust economic activity, predicting positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days as investors anticipate sustained growth and higher corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when GDPC1 shows a sustained upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion phase (GDPC1 growth >3% monthly), elevated demand signals peak growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 5 days as market participants anticipate limited upside potential.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during periods classified as late-cycle expansion.
